0.headline: Swaraj Green Power and Fuel files UDRHP with SEBI, plans to raise Rs 1,100 crore via IPO to pare debt
0.heading: Swaraj Green Power and Fuel files UDRHP with SEBI, plans to raise Rs 1,100 crore via IPO to pare debt
0.intro: Swaraj Green Power and Fuel IPO |  The Maharashtra-based company plans to raise Rs 800 crore through a fresh issue of equity shares, while promoter Ranjeetsingh Hindurao Naik Nimbalkar has proposed to sell shares worth Rs 300 crore via OFS.
0.body:
Swaraj Green Power and Fuel, an ethanol production and sugar manufacturing company, has filed an updated draft red herring prospectus (UDRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), seeking to raise up to Rs 1,100 crore through its maiden public offering.

The Maharashtra-based company, headquartered in Satara, plans to raise Rs 800 crore through a fresh issue of equity shares, while promoter Ranjeetsingh Hindurao Naik Nimbalkar has proposed to sell shares worth Rs 300 crore through an offer-for-sale (OFS).

The company may also consider raising up to Rs 160 crore through a pre-IPO private placement, which would form part of the fresh issue. Accordingly, if the pre-IPO placement is undertaken, the size of the fresh issue will be reduced by the amount raised through the placement.

Swaraj Green Power had initially approached the capital markets by filing its draft offer document through the confidential pre-filing route in March this year. Subsequently, the SEBI cleared draft papers in June 2026.

The company operates an integrated manufacturing facility in Maharashtra with a zero liquid discharge system. The facility has an installed sugarcane crushing capacity of 7,500 tonnes of cane per day (TCD), a cogeneration unit with a capacity of 636 MW and a distillery unit with a capacity of 500 kilolitres per day (KLPD).

Click Here To Read All IPO News

According to the CARE report, the company is the second-largest player in Maharashtra in terms of molasses- and grain-based (maize/corn) feedstock utilisation.

Swaraj Green Power proposes to utilise Rs 620.8 crore from the net proceeds of the fresh issue towards repayment of debt against its outstanding borrowings of Rs 747.4 crore as of September 2026. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

On the financial front, Swaraj Green Power reported a standalone profit of Rs 13.1 crore on revenue of Rs 352.5 crore for the three months ended June 2026. For the financial year ended March 2026, the company reported a profit of Rs 25.3 crore on revenue of Rs 1,021.6 crore.

Centrum Broking and InCred Capital Financial Services have been appointed as the merchant bankers to manage the Swaraj Green Power and Fuel IPO.

1.headline: Sterlite Electric, Beauty Garage, Nobel Hygiene, Svatantra Microfin among 8 companies to receive SEBI nod for IPOs
1.heading: Sterlite Electric, Beauty Garage, Nobel Hygiene, Svatantra Microfin among 8 companies to receive SEBI nod for IPOs
1.intro: SEBI issued observations on the draft offer documents of Emerald Jewel Industry India, Svatantra Microfin, Nobel Hygiene, MP Steel (India) and Kataria Dhulchand Pannalal Jewellers on November 27.
1.body:
Ananya Birla-led Svatantra Microfin, Sterlite Electric, Beauty Garage and Nobel Hygiene are among eight companies that have received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to proceed with their initial public offering (IPO) plans. The capital markets regulator also cleared the draft offer documents of Gaurik Fashions, Emerald Jewel Industry India, MP Steel (India) and Kataria Dhulchand Pannalal Jewellers.

Sterlite Electric filed its draft offer document with SEBI in October 2025 to raise funds through an IPO, followed by Gaurik Fashions in May 2026. Emerald Jewel Industry India and Beauty Garage approached the regulator with their draft red herring prospectuses (DRHPs) in July 2026. Meanwhile, Svatantra Microfin, Nobel Hygiene, MP Steel (India) and Kataria Dhulchand Pannalal Jewellers filed their draft IPO papers in August 2026.

SEBI issued its observations on Sterlite Electric's draft offer document on November 20, followed by those of Gaurik Fashions and Beauty Garage on November 26. The regulator issued observations on the draft offer documents of Emerald Jewel Industry India, Svatantra Microfin, Nobel Hygiene, MP Steel (India) and Kataria Dhulchand Pannalal Jewellers on November 27, according to the processing status of draft offer documents published for the week ended November 27.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

The issuance of observations on a DRHP filed through the normal route allows a company to proceed with its IPO within the next 12 months and raise funds from the capital markets. Companies that file their offer documents through the confidential pre-filing route have an 18-month window to proceed with their IPO plans.

Sterlite Electric, part of the Vedanta Group, is looking to raise around Rs 1,500 crore through its initial public offering (IPO), according to media reports. The IPO comprises fresh issue of 77.93 lakh shares and an OFS of 77.96 lakh shares by existing shareholders including promoter Twins Star Overseas. The company manufactures overhead conductors, power cables and optical ground wires, provides power cable solutions and offers master system integration services. It plans to use the IPO proceeds to fund its growth plans and reduce debt.

Ananya Birla-promoted non-banking financial company (NBFC) Svatantra Microfin plans to raise up to Rs 3,000 crore through its public issue. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth Rs 1,500 crore, while global private equity firm Advent International-controlled Valiocina and Renuka Ramnath-founded Multiples Alternate Asset Management will sell shares worth Rs 1,064.8 crore and Rs 435.2 crore, respectively, through the offer-for-sale (OFS) route.

Quadria Capital- and Sixth Sense Ventures-backed Nobel Hygiene, which manufactures diapers and other absorbent hygiene products under brands including Friends and Teddyy, aims to raise Rs 150 crore through a fresh issue of shares. The public issue will also include an OFS of 1.55 crore equity shares by existing shareholders.

Besides promoters Kamal Kumar Johari and his wife, Kamini Johari, the selling shareholders in the OFS will include Quadria Capital-managed Orbit Investment Holdings, Sixth Sense Ventures and Bennett Trading LLP.

Mumbai-based Beauty Garage, a haircare solutions provider behind brands such as K9, Botoliss, Shea and Scalp Sense, has approached the capital markets to raise up to Rs 125 crore through a fresh issue of shares. The IPO will also include an OFS of 78.36 lakh shares by its promoters, Jigar Babubhai Ravaria and Mahesh Babubhai Ravaria.

Fashion and lifestyle brands retailer Gaurik Fashions has tapped the capital markets to fund its expansion through new store openings and repay debt. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of 62 lakh shares and an OFS of 8 lakh shares. Aries Opportunities Fund will be the sole selling shareholder in the OFS.

Gujarat-based stainless steel products manufacturer MP Steel (India) plans to raise Rs 95 crore through a fresh issue of shares to set up a manufacturing unit for billets and meet its working capital requirements. Its promoters will also offload 23.07 lakh shares through the OFS route.

Madhya Pradesh-based Kataria Dhulchand Pannalal Jewellers, which operates under the brand name Kataria Jewellers, has approached the capital markets to raise fresh capital through an issue of 1.6 crore shares. The company plans to use the proceeds primarily to expand its store network and repay debt.

Coimbatore-based jewellery manufacturer Emerald Jewel Industry India has filed its draft offer documents through the confidential pre-filing route. Its proposed IPO is expected to comprise a combination of a fresh issue of shares and an OFS by existing shareholders.

2.headline: Ananya Birla-led Svatantra Microfin gets SEBI nod for Rs 3,000-crore IPO
2.heading: Ananya Birla-led Svatantra Microfin gets SEBI nod for Rs 3,000-crore IPO
2.intro: Issue comprises a fresh issue of Rs 1,500 crore and an offer for sale of an equal amount; proceeds will be used to strengthen the lender's capital base.
2.body:
Ananya Birla-led Svatantra Microfin has received observations from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its proposed Rs 3,000-crore initial public offering (IPO), taking the company a step closer to its public listing.

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 1,500 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs 1,500 crore. The company will use the proceeds from the fresh issue to augment its Tier-I capital base to meet future capital requirements, including funding business expansion and onward lending.

Business profile

Svatantra Microfin is the second-largest non-banking financial company-microfinance institution (NBFC-MFI) in India by microfinance assets under management (AUM), as of March 31, 2026.

Its microfinance AUM grew at a compound annual growth rate of 20.87 percent between FY24 and FY26, reaching Rs 21,093 crore at the end of March 2026, compared with Rs 14,438 crore in March 2024.

The company reported a gross Stage 3 ratio of 1.19 percent in FY26, down from 2.24 percent in FY25. It had 2,123 branches across 20 states and 394 districts, serving over 42.6 lakh active microfinance borrowers as of March 31, 2026.

The IPO comes after Svatantra's amalgamation with Chaitanya India Fin Credit, effective March 21, 2026, which strengthened its presence in southern India and expanded its pan-India footprint.

The equity shares will be listed on the BSE and the National Stock Exchange. Axis Capital, Avendus Capital, IIFL Capital Services, Kotak Mahindra Capital and SBI Capital Markets are the book-running lead managers.
